title: Rename many files: replace spaces with underscores and use lowercase
summary: Renames every plain file in a folder so that spaces become underscores and letters become small. First you see the planned new names, then you apply them. A file whose new name is already taken is skipped, never overwritten.

steps.explain: Preview only: print the mv command for each plain file whose name would change. Nothing is renamed yet. Two spaces become two underscores, so 'Other  Doc.pdf' becomes 'other__doc.pdf'. Change the plan if a name looks wrong.
steps.cmd: (cd <DIR> && for f in *; do [ -f "$f" ] || continue; n="${f// /_}"; n="${n,,}"; [ "$f" != "$n" ] && printf 'mv -- %q %q\n' "$f" "$n"; done)
steps.expect: Lines such as: mv -- My\ File.TXT my_file.txt  (the backslashes show the space in the old name).

steps.explain: Apply the renames. A file is renamed only if its new name is free; otherwise the line 'skipped, name taken' is printed. Folders are not touched.
steps.cmd: (cd <DIR> && for f in *; do [ -f "$f" ] || continue; n="${f// /_}"; n="${n,,}"; [ "$f" = "$n" ] && continue; if [ -e "$n" ]; then echo "skipped, name taken: $f"; else mv -n -- "$f" "$n"; fi; done)
steps.expect: Usually no output. Only the skipped lines appear, for names that were already taken.

placeholders.name: DIR
placeholders.description: Same folder as in the preview step

steps.explain: Check the new names in the folder.
steps.expect: One name per line, all in lowercase, with underscores instead of spaces.

prerequisites: A copy of the folder, or a backup, if the names matter to other programs

rollback.explain: Rename the files back. The preview lines show each old and new name, so reverse each pair with mv. Keep the preview output if you want an undo list.

warnings: The shell cannot undo a rename. Run the preview step first and read every line.
Programs, scripts and links that use the old names will stop finding the files.
Only plain files are renamed. Folders keep their names.
